doc.title: Bruce Johnstone interviewed by Monk Rowe, Dunkirk, New York, October 11, 2013

title: Max Stewart teaches him slap tongue
summary: A baritone player from England in New Zealand showed him how to slap tongue.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Yeah. Some guy in New Zealand showed me how to slap tongue. His name was Max Stewart, and he was a baritone player from England, who’d come to New Zealand and started a jewelry store. And he had been a professional musician in England and he’d recorded all of Rudy Wiedoeft’s material on baritone. So he did “Oodles of Noodles” and “Saxophobia,” and all those old corny things. And he showed me how to do this slap tongue thing. And it’s not about hitting here, it’s about hitting back. Like right off the © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -14-

roof of your mouth, so, and you have the reed in there. So you’re shutting the reed, and then the pressure behind it as you open the reed pops it. And you have just enough power to go through it to make the reed vibrate.
